name: PV central inverter
summary: A large solar inverter fed from DC combiner boxes, usually paired with its own medium-voltage transformer.
description: A central inverter converts the combined output of many PV strings at a single location. Strings are first paralleled in DC combiner boxes, which feed DC recombiners and then the inverter. Ratings run from several hundred kilowatts to several megawatts, and the inverter usually sits in a skid with a medium-voltage step-up transformer and switchgear.

Single-line diagrams show the DC combiner network converging on one inverter block, the inverter output to a low-voltage winding of the skid transformer, and the medium-voltage ring main unit. Dual inverters sharing one three-winding transformer are also common.

A central inverter fault takes a large part of the plant offline, and the DC cabling distances are long. The symbol does not show DC earthing arrangement or insulation monitoring, which differ between plants and must be stated separately.
